result.title: Turns Matter: Advancing Streaming Video RL via Turn-Level Credit
result.summary: Streaming video understanding requires models to repeatedly decide whether to respond or continue observing. Recently, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has been applied to this setting, with existing approaches emphasizing reward design while retaining a single trajectory-level advantage across turns. Such shared credit can reinforce redundant replies after earlier successes and discourage useful follow-ups after earlier failures. We propose TurnWise, a turn-level GRPO framework that aligns learning with individual streaming decisions. TurnWise addresses the mismatch between trajectory-level feedback and turn-level interaction, promoting informative responses and reducing redundancy. Specifically, turn-level credit assignment uses silence-completed prefix scoring to construct group-relative advantages from each decision's remaining return, separating its learning signal from earlier rewards. Turn-mean policy optimization averages token losses within each turn and then across turns, giving response and waiting decisions equal weight regardless of output length. These complementary designs improve streaming policy learning without a learned critic or additional rollouts. Extensive experiments show our method outperforms prior RL approaches for streaming video understanding.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TurnWise，针对流式视频理解中「作答还是继续观察」的逐轮决策，用 silence-completed prefix scoring 从每步剩余回报构造轮级 group-relative advantage，并在轮内、轮间对 token loss 取平均，以避免轨迹级共享优势带来的冗余回答或抑制后续追问。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及 STOP 式停止/继续观察决策及其训练信号分配：轮级信用分配与轮均值策略优化可供核查能否区分「等待」与「作答」两类决策的贡献，并评估其在流式视觉证据获取中的收益与成本权衡。
